claims.text: As-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type thin films or nanoribbons have broadened magnetic hysteresis and a muted magnetocaloric response.
Limited heat-transfer rates cause the broadened hysteresis and muted magnetocaloric response of these FeMnNiGeSi-type nanostructures.
A patterned micro-heater or thermal-management layer can be integrated adjacent to or beneath the nanostructure with controllable power density.
The proposed cycles use applied magnetic fields below 100 mT and temperatures near the magnetic phase transition.
The selected cycling rates stress nanoscale heat-transfer limitations.
The integrated micro-heater enhances local thermal gradients at the interface.
The enhanced interfacial thermal gradients facilitate faster thermal relaxation.
The enhanced interfacial thermal gradients modify magnetic-domain reconfiguration.
Active micro-heater operation accelerates local heat dissipation and reduces thermal lag during magnetic-field cycling.
Reduced thermal lag sharpens the magnetic phase transition.
Reduced thermal lag decreases delay in domain reconfiguration and reduces domain-wall pinning.
Micro-heater-equipped nanostructures will have lower coercivity and a narrower or smaller-area hysteresis loop than the as-deposited control.
Micro-heater-equipped nanostructures will exhibit a larger peak magnetocaloric entropy change than the as-deposited control.
The proposed effect is expected specifically below 100 mT and near the magnetic phase transition, and to be less pronounced at higher fields or away from the transition.
Compositional heterogeneity can influence magnetic interactions or domain-related hysteresis behavior in compositionally complex magnetic materials.
Competing interfacial phenomena could influence magnetic-domain dynamics and hysteresis.
Failure to obtain both a statistically significant hysteresis reduction and a corresponding entropy-change increase relative to the control would falsify the proposed thermal-management mechanism.
